cues.en: This is the Happy Pod from the BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 这里是 BBC 世界服务的《Happy Pod》。

cues.en: I'm Holly Gibbs, and in this edition, meet Mina and Minal.
cues.zh: 我是霍莉·吉布斯。本期节目认识米娜和米纳尔。

cues.en: It's like all those 30 years we've been apart, we've never been apart.
cues.zh: 感觉这分开的30年里，我们从未真正分开。

cues.en: It's like we're picking up after that, and it feels really strange, but very good. It feels like home.
cues.zh: 就像我们从那时继续走下去，感觉很奇妙，却又非常美好，像回到了家。

cues.en: The girls who became best friends, only to discover they are actually biological sisters.
cues.zh: 两个女孩成为最好的朋友，却发现彼此其实是亲姐妹。

cues.en: Also on this podcast, this project is not just about teaching music.
cues.zh: 本期节目还将介绍：这个项目不只是教音乐。

cues.en: We're bringing to the world's attention this place, these kids—the orchestra who play instruments made from rubbish.
cues.zh: 我们要让世界关注这个地方和这些孩子，以及用垃圾制作乐器演奏的管弦乐团。

cues.en: Plus, the grandmother and grandson duo healing their relationship through travel.
cues.zh: 还有一对祖母和孙子，通过旅行修复彼此的关系。

cues.en: And when you think about it, it's pretty logical.
cues.zh: 仔细想想，这很合乎逻辑。

cues.en: When we're out of the office, it's just empty space, and a lot of space, and that can be comfy.
cues.zh: 我们不在办公室时，那里只是空着的大片空间，也可以住得很舒服。

cues.en: The offices in France which welcome people experiencing homelessness to stay.
cues.zh: 法国的一些办公室欢迎无家可归者在那里留宿。

cues.en: We start with a remarkable DNA discovery which revealed that two best friends were actually biological sisters.
cues.zh: 我们先来看一项惊人的 DNA 发现：两个最好的朋友原来是亲姐妹。

cues.en: Mina and Minal were both born in India. They were then adopted by different families and raised near each other in the Netherlands.
cues.zh: 米娜和米纳尔都出生于印度，后来被不同家庭收养，在荷兰彼此相近的地方长大。

cues.en: It was only when they met by chance that they realised their similarities, as Amelia Clarke reports.
cues.zh: 直到一次偶然相遇，她们才意识到彼此有多么相像。阿米莉娅·克拉克报道。

cues.en: “Who's this?” “My sister.” Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen were both born in the early 1980s.
cues.zh: “这是谁？”“我妹妹。”米娜·格尔廷克和米纳尔·蒂森都出生于20世纪80年代初。

cues.en: They were adopted from two different orphanages in Mumbai within months of their birth.
cues.zh: 她们出生后几个月内，分别从孟买的两家孤儿院被收养。

cues.en: They first met in their early teens at an event hosted by an adoption agency.
cues.zh: 她们十几岁时第一次见面，地点是收养机构举办的一场活动。

cues.en: Their parents had used the agency, and the girls were struck by their uncanny similarities in appearance and mannerisms.
cues.zh: 她们的父母曾联系过这家机构；两个女孩惊讶于彼此外貌和举止的惊人相似。

cues.en: They promised to stay in touch and spent years writing letters to each other.
cues.zh: 她们约定保持联系，多年来互相写信。

cues.en: They often addressed each other as “sis”, despite not knowing the truth about their relation.
cues.zh: 她们常称对方为“姐妹”，却不知道两人的真实关系。

cues.en: Minal and Mina lost contact after Minal moved to France and Mina had a baby, until earlier this year when Minal decided to take a DNA test.
cues.zh: 米纳尔搬到法国、米娜生下孩子后，两人失去了联系，直到今年早些时候米纳尔决定做 DNA 检测。

cues.en: I was home alone, and then I got the pop-up on my phone. It said, “Your results from DNA MyHeritage are ready.”
cues.zh: 当时我独自在家，手机弹出一条通知：“你的 DNA MyHeritage 检测结果已出。”

cues.en: So I opened it, and then there was written, “Mina, sister.”
cues.zh: 我打开通知，上面写着：“米娜，姐妹。”

cues.en: And I didn't realise it was Mina that I know.
cues.zh: 我没意识到那就是我认识的米娜。

cues.en: Minal messaged Mina on social media, asking if she remembered her.
cues.zh: 米纳尔在社交媒体上给米娜留言，问她是否记得自己。

cues.en: Mina had tried to do a DNA test in 2017 but was told she had no matches.
cues.zh: 米娜2017年曾试着做 DNA 检测，却被告知没有匹配结果。

cues.en: But the test Minal did confirmed the girls were 100% sisters, which means they share the same biological mother and father.
cues.zh: 但米纳尔的检测确认两人是百分之百的亲姐妹，也就是说，她们拥有同一位生母和生父。

cues.en: Last month, the girls met for the first time since finding out they were related.
cues.zh: 上个月，得知彼此有亲缘关系后，两个女孩第一次见面。

cues.en: Minal says it's what she's dreamed of.
cues.zh: 米纳尔说，这正是她梦寐以求的事。

cues.en: I've always been surrounded by many people who love me and who took care of me. But something inside of me, I've always felt very lonely.
cues.zh: 我身边一直有许多爱我、照顾我的人。但在内心深处，我始终感到非常孤独。

cues.en: And, yeah, I always hoped to find some biological family somewhere.
cues.zh: 我一直希望能在某处找到亲生家人。

cues.en: I always said, “Yes, I would love to see if there's my biological mother,” but even more brothers or sisters.
cues.zh: 我总说：“我很想知道亲生母亲是否还在”，更想找到兄弟姐妹。

cues.en: And now this happens. So inside it was like, now I don't feel alone anymore.
cues.zh: 而现在这一切真的发生了。那一刻我觉得，自己终于不再孤单。

cues.en: For Mina, it's as if no time has passed. It's like all those 30 years we've been apart.
cues.zh: 对米娜来说，就像时间从未流逝；就像那分开的30年从未发生。

cues.en: We've never been apart. It's like we're picking up after that, and it feels really strange but very good. It feels like home.
cues.zh: 我们从未真正分开。就像从那时继续走下去，感觉很奇妙，却非常美好，像回到了家。

cues.en: Yeah, yeah. It's like we don't live together; we have very different lives.
cues.zh: 是的。我们并不住在一起，生活也截然不同。

cues.en: But when I see you, it's like I'm home.
cues.zh: 但每当我见到你，就像回到了家。

cues.en: I feel finally complete, and that's the puzzle piece in my heart.
cues.zh: 我终于感到完整了，你就是我心里的那块拼图。

cues.en: And yeah, I know that it's a lot, but it feels really good, yeah.
cues.zh: 我知道这一切分量很重，但感觉真的非常好。

cues.en: Since finding out, Mina and Minal have spoken almost every day.
cues.zh: 得知真相后，米娜和米纳尔几乎每天交谈。

cues.en: They've met each other's husbands and children, and the families they were adopted into.
cues.zh: 她们见过彼此的丈夫和孩子，也见过收养她们的家庭。

cues.en: One day, they hope to go back to the orphanage where the story began.
cues.zh: 有一天，她们希望回到这个故事开始的那家孤儿院。

cues.en: But for now, the sisters say the fact they're siblings is something that is still sinking in.
cues.zh: 但现在，姐妹俩说，她们确实是姐妹这一事实仍在慢慢被自己接受。

cues.en: That was Amelia Clarke reporting.
cues.zh: 以上是阿米莉娅·克拉克的报道。

cues.en: To Paraguay next, and an orchestra which plays rubbish, quite literally.
cues.zh: 接下来去往巴拉圭，认识一支字面意义上演奏垃圾的管弦乐团。

cues.en: All of their instruments are made of scrap found at landfill. Branca Lessa de Sá has been finding out more.
cues.zh: 他们的乐器全由垃圾填埋场找到的废料制成。布兰卡·莱萨·德·萨带来报道。

cues.en: That's Wuiwi Lopez, playing his violin.
cues.zh: 那是维维·洛佩斯在演奏小提琴。

cues.en: It sounds just like any other violin, but it looks distinctly different.
cues.zh: 听起来和普通小提琴一样，但外观明显不同。

cues.en: Rather than the usual mahogany wood, Wuiwi's instrument is a haphazard combination of colours and textures, and that's because it's made from rubbish.
cues.zh: 维维的乐器不是用常见的桃花心木制成，而是由各种颜色和质感杂乱组合而成，因为它来自垃圾。

cues.en: Wuiwi is talking to me from his studio in Paraguay.
cues.zh: 维维正在巴拉圭的工作室里接受我的采访。

cues.en: Here, he turns scraps of metal, wood, paper and plastic into music.
cues.zh: 他把金属、木头、纸张和塑料废料变成音乐。

cues.en: He works with Favio Chavez, the founder and conductor of the Recycled Orchestra of Cateura.
cues.zh: 他与卡特乌拉回收乐团的创办人兼指挥法维奥·查韦斯合作。

cues.en: Cateura lies on the outskirts of Paraguay's capital, Asunción.
cues.zh: 卡特乌拉位于巴拉圭首都亚松森郊外。

cues.en: It's a vast, sprawling landfill. Every day, about 3 million pounds of solid waste get dumped here.
cues.zh: 那里是一片广阔的垃圾填埋场。每天约有300万磅固体废物被倾倒在这里。

cues.en: Thousands of families live in and around Cateura.
cues.zh: 数千个家庭生活在卡特乌拉及其周边。

cues.en: They survive by sorting the rubbish for things they can sell.
cues.zh: 他们靠分拣垃圾，寻找可以出售的物品维生。

cues.en: Kids regularly get pulled out of school to help.
cues.zh: 孩子们经常被迫辍学来帮忙。

cues.en: Theirs is a childhood marked by the sound of garbage trucks and plastic bags, or was until Favio came along.
cues.zh: 他们的童年曾伴随着垃圾车和塑料袋的声音，直到法维奥的到来。

cues.en: When Favio started working in Cateura in 2006, he was an environmental technician helping locals classify what they found in the waste.
cues.zh: 法维奥于2006年开始在卡泰乌拉工作，作为环境技术员帮助当地人分类垃圾中的物品。

cues.en: When he first arrived, he was shocked by what he saw. I met families whose
cues.zh: 他初到那里时，被眼前的景象震惊了。我遇到一些家庭，他们的

cues.en: most basic necessities weren't being met.
cues.zh: 连最基本的生活必需品都得不到满足。

cues.en: The children in this place didn't have the options for study or ways to use their free time positively.
cues.zh: 这里的孩子没有学习的机会，也没有积极利用空闲时间的方式。

cues.en: Favio wanted to help and knew there was only one way he could.
cues.zh: 法维奥想提供帮助，并知道自己只有一个办法。

cues.en: What I knew at that time and had experience in was music, to offer
cues.zh: 我当时所了解、也有经验的领域是音乐，所以可以提供

cues.en: the possibility of music lessons, as I was already a music teacher back home.
cues.zh: 音乐课的机会，因为我在家乡已经是一名音乐老师。

cues.en: He began to offer lessons to the children of Cateura, using donated instruments.
cues.zh: 他开始用捐赠的乐器给卡泰乌拉的孩子们上课。

cues.en: But the classes proved so popular, they soon ran out.
cues.zh: 但课程大受欢迎，很快就招满了。

cues.en: Instead of turning people away, Favio had an idea: to make instruments out of the rubbish from the dump.
cues.zh: 法维奥没有拒绝人们，而是想出了一个办法：用垃圾场里的废弃物制作乐器。

cues.en: It was a long process and it continues to be, as we're still refining it.
cues.zh: 这是一个漫长的过程，而且仍在继续，因为我们还在不断改进。

cues.en: Despite the difficulties, they eventually did manage. And thus was born the Recycled Orchestra of Cateura.
cues.zh: 尽管困难重重，他们最终还是成功了。卡泰乌拉回收乐团就这样诞生了。

cues.en: The orchestra has now been playing for over 20 years and gained international acclaim.
cues.zh: 这支乐团如今演奏了20多年，并赢得了国际声誉。

cues.en: They have travelled and performed in countries across the world.
cues.zh: 他们走遍世界各国演出。

cues.en: More recently, a musical was made about their story.
cues.zh: 最近，还有一部音乐剧讲述了他们的故事。

cues.en: It premiered this summer in Atlanta.
cues.zh: 音乐剧今年夏天在亚特兰大首演。

cues.en: The production was a success, and next year they'll be performing at Carnegie Hall.
cues.zh: 这部作品取得了成功，明年他们还将在卡内基音乐厅演出。

cues.en: But when Wuiwi first joined the orchestra, he could never have imagined its future success. At the time, they had no rehearsal space or shows lined up.
cues.zh: 但乌伊维刚加入乐团时，绝不可能想象它会取得这样的成功。那时，他们没有自己的排练场地，也没有安排演出。

cues.en: It really was a passion project, something from the heart.
cues.zh: 这确实是一个发自内心的热爱项目。

cues.en: Wuiwi had received free music lessons from Favio when he was at school.
cues.zh: 乌伊维上学时曾接受法维奥提供的免费音乐课。

cues.en: For him, who had always loved music but lacked the means to pursue it, the lessons were transformational.
cues.zh: 他一直热爱音乐，却没有条件追求音乐；这些课程改变了他的人生。

cues.en: So when he found out about the project, he immediately knew he wanted to help.
cues.zh: 所以得知这个项目后，他立刻就知道自己想要帮忙。

cues.en: I really admired it because it reminded me of me, and I felt a lot of empathy and connection
cues.zh: 我非常钦佩这个项目，因为它让我想起自己；我对这些孩子有很强的共情和联系，

cues.en: to these kids who gave everything they had to make their dreams come true.
cues.zh: 他们倾尽所有，让自己的梦想成真。

cues.en: Now, as well as teaching music lessons and playing, Wuiwi makes and repairs all the instruments used by the orchestra.
cues.zh: 如今，除了教音乐和演奏，乌伊维还制作、修理乐团使用的所有乐器。

cues.en: But for both Favio and Wuiwi, the project is about more than just music or recycling.
cues.zh: 但对法维奥和乌伊维来说，这个项目不只是音乐或回收。

cues.en: This project is not just about teaching music; we're bringing to the world's attention this place, these kids.
cues.zh: 这个项目不只是教音乐；我们还要让全世界关注这个地方和这些孩子。

cues.en: When a child stands out for a skill—in this case, music—they cease to be anonymous.
cues.zh: 当一个孩子凭某项技能脱颖而出——在这里是音乐——他们就不再默默无闻。

cues.en: They cease to be someone that…
cues.zh: 他们不再是一个……

cues.en: doesn't matter; they become someone important.
cues.zh: 无足轻重的人，而会成为重要的人。

cues.en: That was Branca Lessa de Sa reporting.
cues.zh: 以上是布兰卡·莱萨·德·萨的报道。

cues.en: A man and his grandmother have been on a mission to visit every national park in the United States, before going on safari trips around the world.
cues.zh: 一名男子和他的祖母立志走遍美国每座国家公园，然后再去世界各地进行野外旅行。

cues.en: For them, it wasn't about the sights, but healing their relationship.
cues.zh: 对他们来说，重点不在风景，而在修复彼此的关系。

cues.en: Brad and Joy Ryan had not spoken in ten years, but now they have rekindled.
cues.zh: 布拉德和乔伊·瑞安十年没有说过话，但如今重新修复了关系。

cues.en: Brad has even written a book about their adventures.
cues.zh: 布拉德甚至还写了一本关于他们冒险经历的书。

cues.en: Brad and Grandma Joy have been speaking to my colleague, Kassa Aloum.
cues.zh: 布拉德和乔伊奶奶接受了我的同事卡萨·阿卢姆的采访。

cues.en: Well, it started when I was 85. He called up, wondering if I wanted to go camping, and I said yes.
cues.zh: 这段经历始于我85岁时。他打电话问我想不想去露营，我说想。

cues.en: So away we went, and we got there in the rain. It was quite a trip, I can tell you that.
cues.zh: 于是我们出发了，在雨中抵达那里。那真是一趟特别的旅程。

cues.en: I held the umbrella over him while he put the tent together.
cues.zh: 他搭帐篷时，我替他撑着伞。

cues.en: And then the air mattress—I kept falling off it, so I said to heck
cues.zh: 还有充气床垫——我总是从上面掉下来，所以我说，管它呢，

cues.en: with it, I'll just sleep on the ground. Brad, you know how to treat…
cues.zh: 我就睡地上吧。布拉德，你知道该怎样对待……

cues.en: a woman, don't you?
cues.zh: 一个女人，对吧？

cues.en: You know, Grandma Joy is cut from a different cloth.
cues.zh: 你知道，乔伊奶奶是个与众不同的人。

cues.en: I will admit, when we were driving down and I was looking at her hands, I thought, wow, I forgot she's an old woman.
cues.zh: 我得承认，开车时看着她的双手，我心想：哇，我都忘了她是个老人。

cues.en: Because she, you know, her mind and her spirit are so young.
cues.zh: 因为你知道，她的思想和精神都如此年轻。

cues.en: We had so much fun that weekend, and she blew my expectations out of the water.
cues.zh: 那周末我们玩得非常开心，她远远超出了我的期待。

cues.en: That's why we went there: she'd never seen a mountain.
cues.zh: 这就是我们去那里的原因：她从未见过山。

cues.en: And at age 85, she not only saw her first mountain, she climbed her first mountain as well.
cues.zh: 而且85岁时，她不仅看到了人生中的第一座山，还爬上了人生中的第一座山。

cues.en: That's really why I wanted to keep the magic alive.
cues.zh: 这正是我想让这份魔力延续下去的原因。

cues.en: I didn't intend in the beginning to go to all 63 US National Parks.
cues.zh: 起初，我没打算走遍美国全部63座国家公园。

cues.en: We had no intention of setting a world record.
cues.zh: 我们无意创造世界纪录。

cues.en: She became the oldest person in the world to begin and complete a circuit to all 63 US National Parks.
cues.zh: 她成为世界上开始并完成美国63座国家公园之旅的最年长者。

cues.en: But it really just began as a way to repair our relationship.
cues.zh: 但这一切最初真的只是为了修复我们的关系。

cues.en: We hadn't spoken in ten years at the beginning of this journey, and now we're best friends.
cues.zh: 这段旅程开始时，我们已有十年没说过话；如今我们成了最好的朋友。

cues.en: And Joy, for yourself, spending this time with Brad, how has that been for you, as well as visiting all these places?
cues.zh: 乔伊，对你来说，与布拉德共度这段时光、游览这些地方，感觉如何？

cues.en: We had a lot of things to discuss about.
cues.zh: 我们有很多事情要讨论。

cues.en: We talked about the things we saw outside, and I think we got along pretty good.
cues.zh: 我们聊了聊在外面看到的那些事，我觉得我们相处得很好。

cues.en: When you haven't spoken to each other in ten years, you know, there is a lot of ground that you have to make up.
cues.zh: 你们十年没和彼此说过话，确实有很多隔阂需要弥合。

cues.en: Why was that, by the way? It was a fractious divorce. Her eldest son was my father.
cues.zh: 顺便问一下，为什么会这样？那是一场充满冲突的离婚。她的大儿子是我的父亲。

cues.en: When I was hiking the Appalachian Trail, when I was in my late twenties, we were nearly a decade into our estrangement.
cues.zh: 我二十多岁后期徒步走阿巴拉契亚步道时，我们的疏远已经持续了近十年。

cues.en: I was sleeping next to the stream and thinking about those early childhood memories when she would take me into the local state park.
cues.zh: 我睡在溪流旁，想起童年早期她带我去当地州立公园的那些回忆。

cues.en: And I just felt like I had to try.
cues.zh: 我只是觉得自己必须试一试。

cues.en: When I finished the Appalachian Trail, after six months in the wilderness, I felt like I had to try to reconnect.
cues.zh: 在荒野中度过六个月、走完阿巴拉契亚步道后，我觉得自己必须尝试重新建立联系。

cues.en: And I thought she might slam the door in my face, to be honest, because her feelings were really hurt.
cues.zh: 老实说，我以为她可能会把我拒之门外，因为她的感情确实受到了伤害。

cues.en: It's like any other type of reparation, right?
cues.zh: 这就像其他任何形式的修复，对吧？

cues.en: You don't rebuild a relationship overnight after ten years of not speaking to somebody.
cues.zh: 十年不和一个人说话，不可能一夜之间重建关系。

cues.en: You have to start somewhere, and for us, going back to nature was the most natural place to begin that healing process.
cues.zh: 总得从某个地方开始；对我们来说，回归大自然是开启疗愈过程最自然的起点。

cues.en: And that nature took you all around the world.
cues.zh: 而大自然之旅带着你们走遍了世界。

cues.en: Joy, tell me about some of the places that you've traveled to, all around the world. What's been your favorite place, both of you?
cues.zh: Joy，告诉我你们在世界各地去过哪些地方。你们两个人最喜欢哪里？

cues.en: Well, we started in Kenya, and that was our first international trip.
cues.zh: 我们从肯尼亚开始，那是我们的第一次国际旅行。

cues.en: So after she completed the 63 US national parks, her Instagram followers asked me what the next chapter was going to be.
cues.zh: 她走完美国63座国家公园后，她的 Instagram 粉丝问我，下一章会是什么。

cues.en: And 63 was a big number, and so we thought, what's an epic journey that would be a smaller number?
cues.zh: 63是个很大的数字，所以我们想，什么史诗般的旅程数量会小一些？

cues.en: And so we came up with the seven continents.
cues.zh: 于是我们想到了走遍七大洲。

cues.en: And when I was 20 years old, I had never been overseas, and she took me to the airport.
cues.zh: 我20岁时从未出过国，是她送我去了机场。

cues.en: And I went to Kenya.
cues.zh: 我就去了肯尼亚。

cues.en: And two months after we reached the national park of American Samoa, which was our 63rd and final US national park,
cues.zh: 到达美属萨摩亚国家公园两个月后，那是我们走过的第63座、也是最后一座美国国家公园，

cues.en: she and I ended up going to Kenya.
cues.zh: 我们俩最终去了肯尼亚。

cues.en: And I remember thinking, when we were in the Lamar Valley at Yellowstone National Park,
cues.zh: 我记得我们在黄石国家公园的拉马尔谷时，我曾想，

cues.en: when we were stuck in this bison traffic jam for four hours,
cues.zh: 我们被野牛造成的交通堵塞困住了4个小时，

cues.en: that she would never get to see the great migration of wildebeest and zebra in Africa.
cues.zh: 她大概永远也看不到非洲角马和斑马的大迁徙。

cues.en: But at least she had that memory.
cues.zh: 但至少她有那段回忆。

cues.en: And, you know, my assumption was wrong, and she ended up getting to see the great migration along the Mara River.
cues.zh: 但我的想法错了，她最终看到了马拉河沿岸的大迁徙。

cues.en: And so, for me, that was just a living, breathing example.
cues.zh: 所以对我来说，那就是一个活生生的例子。

cues.en: That we can manifest these seemingly impossible dreams if two hearts are willing to go along for the ride.
cues.zh: 只要两颗心愿意一起踏上旅程，我们就能实现那些看似不可能的梦想。

cues.en: What about you? What was your favorite country, the favorite place that you visited overseas?
cues.zh: 那你呢？你最喜欢哪个国家，最喜欢在海外去过的哪个地方？

cues.en: Oh, I think when we went over and helped the rhinos.
cues.zh: 我想是我们去帮助犀牛的那次。

cues.en: We went over there and there were several people with us.
cues.zh: 我们去了那里，当时还有几个人和我们一起。

cues.en: And it was an amazing experience. It was quite a big operation.
cues.zh: 那是一次奇妙的经历，也是规模相当大的行动。

cues.en: There were airplanes and helicopters, and truckloads of young men that helped.
cues.zh: 有飞机、直升机，还有一车车前来帮忙的年轻人。

cues.en: There'll be lots of people listening to you with a smile on their face.
cues.zh: 很多听众都会面带微笑听你说这些。

cues.en: What would you say to anyone who hasn't travelled that much in their life?
cues.zh: 你想对那些一生中没怎么旅行的人说些什么？

cues.en: If you get a chance to go, go.
cues.zh: 如果有机会出发，就去吧。

cues.en: Somebody asks you to go to someplace, don't say no, say yes,
cues.zh: 有人邀请你去某个地方时，不要说不，要说好，

cues.en: because the next day you'll say, 'Daggone it, I wish I'd said yes and not no.'
cues.zh: 因为第二天你会说：“真该答应，而不是拒绝。”

cues.en: You know, the older you get, the faster time flies.
cues.zh: 你知道，人越老，时间过得越快。

cues.en: So I am getting close to the end, so I am not saying no to nothing; I do everything I can.
cues.zh: 我已经接近人生终点，所以什么都不拒绝，能做的我都会去做。

cues.en: That was Brad Ryan and Grandma Joy.
cues.zh: 刚才是布拉德·瑞安和乔伊奶奶。

cues.en: Coming up on the Happy Pod:
cues.zh: 《快乐播客》接下来：

cues.en: I firmly believe that this is a sport because of the quick decision-making you have to make with your brain.
cues.zh: 我坚信这是一项运动，因为你必须用大脑快速做出决定。

cues.en: Massively has benefits in terms of slowing down the illness.
cues.zh: 这对延缓病情有巨大益处。

cues.en: The table tennis club helping people with Parkinson's disease.
cues.zh: 乒乓球俱乐部帮助帕金森病患者。

cues.en: You're listening to the Happy Pod.
cues.zh: 你正在收听《快乐播客》。

cues.en: In western France, one charity is helping those experiencing homelessness.
cues.zh: 在法国西部，一家慈善机构正在帮助无家可归者。

cues.en: They are partnering with businesses to open up unused office space, so it can be used as overnight accommodation.
cues.zh: 他们与企业合作，开放闲置办公空间，把它用作过夜住宿。

cues.en: Alex Collins has been to Nantes to find out more.
cues.zh: 亚历克斯·柯林斯前往南特了解更多情况。

cues.en: I'm meeting Frédéric at the place where he lives. It's not your standard accommodation.
cues.zh: 我在弗雷德里克居住的地方见到他。这不是普通的住宿。

cues.en: It's in the office of a software company called Ypresia.
cues.zh: 这里位于一家名为 Ypresia 的软件公司的办公室内。

cues.en: He takes me through the modern open-plan office, past workers at their desks, to the room he sleeps in at night.
cues.zh: 他带我穿过现代化的开放式办公室，经过办公桌旁的员工，来到他夜里睡觉的房间。

cues.en: Here's my stuff: my detergent to do my washing and a bottle of water.
cues.zh: 这是我的东西：洗衣服用的洗涤剂，还有一瓶水。

cues.en: I don't have many things.
cues.zh: 我的东西不多。

cues.en: It's a modest space with plain white walls, and at the far end is a large desk with two computers, which in the day are used by workers.
cues.zh: 这是一个朴素的空间，墙是白色的；尽头有一张大桌子，桌上的两台电脑白天供员工使用。

cues.en: The biggest object in the room is a rectangular box, which looks at first like an office cabinet, but to my surprise, it contains a folded-out bed.
cues.zh: 房间里最大的物件是一个矩形箱子，乍看像办公柜，但令我惊讶的是，里面藏着一张折叠床。

cues.en: Okay, can you just show me the bed?
cues.zh: 好，你能给我看看这张床吗？

cues.en: The bed is being pulled down. It's on the side of a wall and it just flips down. It's a very clever use of space.
cues.zh: 床被拉了下来。它装在墙边，直接翻下。这样利用空间非常巧妙。

cues.en: On the opposite side of the wall to the bed is a modest cabinet, where Frédéric keeps his small number of possessions.
cues.zh: 床另一侧的墙边有一个小柜子，弗雷德里克把少量物品放在那里。

cues.en: On top of that are some ingredients for cooking.
cues.zh: 柜子上放着一些烹饪食材。

cues.en: So you've also got some food there. You've got a lemon.
cues.zh: 所以你这里也有食物。你有一颗柠檬。

cues.en: Yes, I also have some pistachios and some baby onions.
cues.zh: 是的，我还有开心果和小洋葱。

cues.en: Do you want to show us where you cook?
cues.zh: 你想带我们看看你在哪里做饭吗？

cues.en: We head to a kitchen area, which staff members use in the day to eat their lunch. It's the space that Frédéric uses to make dinner in the evening.
cues.zh: 我们来到一个厨房区域，员工白天在那里吃午饭。弗雷德里克晚上就在这里做晚餐。

cues.en: So I have everything I need: a coffee machine, plates, a sink, a fridge.
cues.zh: 所以我需要的都有：咖啡机、盘子、水槽和冰箱。

cues.en: You've got your own shelf on the fridge with a little post-it note with your name.
cues.zh: 你在冰箱上有自己的隔层，还有一张写着你名字的小便签。

cues.en: That's very handy, so everyone knows not to touch your food.
cues.zh: 这很方便，这样大家就知道不能碰你的食物。

cues.en: Occasionally, Frédéric has a coffee with some of the staff.
cues.zh: 弗雷德里克偶尔会和一些员工一起喝咖啡。

cues.en: The ambition of the charity is to help those staying in offices into permanent work and secure housing.
cues.zh: 这个慈善机构的目标，是帮助住在办公室里的人找到长期工作和稳定住房。

cues.en: Bureaux du Cœur believes having a stable place to sleep makes this easier.
cues.zh: Bureaux du Cœur 认为，有一个稳定的睡觉地点会让这一切更容易。

cues.en: Every month, a meeting takes place with the resident and relevant support agencies to ensure everything is staying on track.
cues.zh: 每个月，机构都会与住户和相关支持机构开会，确保一切按计划进行。

cues.en: Tram announcement: Vers Beaujoire. Departure in less than one minute.
cues.zh: 电车广播：开往博若瓦尔。列车将在不到一分钟后出发。

cues.en: I've just got on the number three tram to meet Pierre-Yves Loaëc.
cues.zh: 我刚乘上三号电车，去见皮埃尔-伊夫·洛埃克。

cues.en: He's actually the founder of Bureaux du Cœur.
cues.zh: 他正是 Bureaux du Cœur 的创办人。

cues.en: I'm inside the office of the advertising agency Nobilito.
cues.zh: 我现在在广告公司 Nobilito 的办公室里。

cues.en: It's a business Pierre-Yves runs alongside Bureaux du Cœur, so it's no surprise to find that he's also hosting a person who is homeless there.
cues.zh: 这是皮埃尔-伊夫在运营 Bureaux du Cœur 之余经营的企业，所以他也在这里接待一位无家可归者，并不奇怪。

cues.en: He's been there for a month.
cues.zh: 他已经在那里住了一个月。

cues.en: I am literally in its big office, but in the corner there, it suddenly feels like someone's bedroom.
cues.zh: 我确实就在这间大办公室里，但角落那里突然让人觉得像某人的卧室。

cues.en: A black curtain gives a degree of privacy, but there's also a sofa which is long enough for someone to sleep on.
cues.zh: 黑色窗帘提供了一定隐私，还有一张足够让人睡下的沙发。

cues.en: I can even see the sheets on the bed there.
cues.zh: 我甚至能看到那张床上的床单。

cues.en: To ensure a respectful experience for the guest, offices are inspected by Bureaux du Cœur volunteers in advance.
cues.zh: 为确保住客有受到尊重的体验，Bureaux du Cœur 的志愿者会提前检查办公室。

cues.en: Guests must have access to a toilet and shower, and cooking facilities.
cues.zh: 住客必须能使用卫生间、淋浴和烹饪设施。

cues.en: The scheme has helped over a hundred people, but Pierre-Yves acknowledges it addresses only a small fraction of Nantes's homeless problem.
cues.zh: 这项计划已帮助一百多人，但皮埃尔-伊夫承认，它只解决了南特无家可归问题的一小部分。

cues.en: However, he says the solution goes beyond helping vulnerable people off the streets.
cues.zh: 不过，他说，这个方案的意义不只是帮助弱势群体离开街头。

cues.en: We commissioned a study that confirmed that companies who took part in our scheme had happier employees.
cues.zh: 我们委托的研究证实，参与计划的公司员工更快乐。

cues.en: They were happier than in a standard French office.
cues.zh: 与普通法国办公室相比，他们的员工更快乐。

cues.en: In the end, I find companies do this because they think it's the moral thing to do.
cues.zh: 归根结底，我认为企业这样做，是因为它们觉得这是道德上正确的事。

cues.en: But what does staff in this town office think about the scheme?
cues.zh: 但这间办公室的员工怎么看这项计划呢？

cues.en: Wandering around, I met Claire and asked her what she thought about the office providing space for a person who is homeless.
cues.zh: 我四处走走时遇到了克莱尔，问她如何看待办公室为一名无家可归者提供空间。

cues.en: When you think about it, it's pretty logical. I mean, when we're out of the office, it's just empty space.
cues.zh: 想想看，这其实很合乎逻辑。我的意思是，我们不在办公室时，那里只是空着。

cues.en: And a lot of space, and that can be comfy.
cues.zh: 而且空间很大，也可以很舒适。

cues.en: So if that can help someone in a difficult situation, I say go for it.
cues.zh: 所以，如果这样能帮助处于困境中的人，我支持这么做。

cues.en: That was Alex Collins reporting.
cues.zh: 以上是亚历克斯·柯林斯的报道。

cues.en: Probiotics have long been all the rage in health advice, but now scientists have also discovered they could be good for corals.
cues.zh: 益生菌长期以来在健康建议中很流行，而科学家如今还发现，它们可能对珊瑚有益。

cues.en: Erika Santoro is a microbiologist turned ecologist. She's been testing a probiotic treatment on reefs in the Red Sea.
cues.zh: 埃里卡·桑托罗原是微生物学家，后来成为生态学家。她一直在红海珊瑚礁测试益生菌疗法。

cues.en: She's been speaking to my colleague, Roland Pease.
cues.zh: 她接受了我的同事罗兰·皮斯的采访。

cues.en: Every single organism on the planet hosts bacteria and other microorganisms. This is not different in the ocean as well.
cues.zh: 地球上的每一种生物体内都有细菌和其他微生物。海洋中也是如此。

cues.en: The corals also host a big amount of bacteria and microalgae, so it is a big mix and soup of microorganisms.
cues.zh: 珊瑚也寄居着大量细菌和微藻，因此这是一个由微生物组成的大混合体。

cues.en: The microorganisms live together with these coral hosts.
cues.zh: 这些微生物与珊瑚宿主共同生活。

cues.en: We call this a holobiont because they work together and evolve together as well.
cues.zh: 我们称其为“共生整体”，因为它们共同运作，也共同进化。

cues.en: When there is stress, like rising ocean temperatures, there is a trigger.
cues.zh: 当出现压力，例如海水温度升高时，就会触发某种机制。

cues.en: That trigger causes a lot of stress in the microalgae.
cues.zh: 这种触发机制会让微藻承受很大压力。

cues.en: They produce many compounds that are stressful for everybody, including the coral host.
cues.zh: 微藻会产生许多让所有生物都感到有压力的化合物，包括珊瑚宿主。

cues.en: A couple of processes can happen there: the algae can be expelled by the host.
cues.zh: 那里可能发生几种过程：藻类可能被宿主排出。

cues.en: They can escape, the cell can break apart, and this mutualistic relationship can just break up.
cues.zh: 它们可能逃离，细胞可能解体，这种互利关系也可能随之破裂。

cues.en: But somewhere along the way, you thought that there was some way.
cues.zh: 但在这个过程中，你想到或许有一种办法。

cues.en: Using probiotics—in other words, adding extra bacteria to unhealthy coral—would help them.
cues.zh: 使用益生菌，也就是给不健康的珊瑚添加额外细菌，或许能帮助它们。

cues.en: Yes, so the idea here is we look at the coral and try to understand the beneficial relationships that exist between the coral and the microorganisms.
cues.zh: 是的，我们要观察珊瑚，了解珊瑚与微生物之间存在的有益关系。

cues.en: And we isolate and manipulate those beneficial ones.
cues.zh: 然后分离并处理其中有益的微生物。

cues.en: I am wondering how you do this, because it's a bit different from taking a teaspoon of yogurt. So what's the process?
cues.zh: 我想知道你们是怎么做的，因为这和喝一茶匙酸奶有些不同。具体流程是什么？

cues.en: Currently, we are doing this in the ocean, so we are upscaling from the lab setups and bringing it to the field.
cues.zh: 目前我们在海洋中进行这项工作，把实验室方案扩大规模并带到现场。

cues.en: We culture those beneficial cells, increase them in number, put them in syringes and apply them on top of the coral.
cues.zh: 我们培养这些有益细胞，增加它们的数量，装入注射器，再施加到珊瑚上。

cues.en: So this is going to create kind of a cloud of beneficial bacteria on top of those colonies, and we apply this often.
cues.zh: 这样会在珊瑚群体上方形成一团有益细菌，我们会经常进行施加。

cues.en: So we guarantee that those corals are going to actually take up those bacteria that we are offering to them.
cues.zh: 这样可以确保珊瑚确实吸收我们提供给它们的细菌。

cues.en: What difference did you see between the treated and the untreated coral?
cues.zh: 你观察到接受处理的珊瑚和未处理珊瑚之间有什么差异？

cues.en: So we observe, first of all, some proxies that are related to coral health.
cues.zh: 首先，我们观察一些与珊瑚健康状况相关的指标。

cues.en: One of them is observing how well they are doing this photosynthesis, and we observed that this was decreasing over time when we don't treat them.
cues.zh: 其中一项是观察它们进行光合作用的状况；我们发现，不加处理时，这项指标会随时间下降。

cues.en: But when we applied the probiotics, with time they were actually recovering.
cues.zh: 但施加益生菌后，它们实际上逐渐恢复了。

cues.en: They were actually having better photosynthesis in those colonies that were treated with probiotics.
cues.zh: 接受益生菌处理的珊瑚群体，光合作用也确实变得更好。

cues.en: So we saw a good result.
cues.zh: 所以我们看到了很好的结果。

cues.en: Corals in the world cover a greater area than just the United Kingdom.
cues.zh: 全世界的珊瑚覆盖面积比英国大得多。

cues.en: This would be, if it became practical, a huge effort. What are the steps before you even get that far?
cues.zh: 如果这项技术变得切实可行，规模会非常庞大。在达到那一步之前，还要经历哪些步骤？

cues.en: We have been observing this positive effect and beneficial effect in different coral species, for different reasons.
cues.zh: 我们在不同珊瑚物种上观察到了这种积极、有益的效果，目的各不相同。

cues.en: To protect against bleaching, mortality and disease.
cues.zh: 有的是为了防止白化和死亡，甚至抵御疾病。

cues.en: So we are really getting excited about the results, and we see that it really works.
cues.zh: 所以我们对这些结果非常兴奋，也看到它确实有效。

cues.en: Now, I think our question is not if it has an effect or not, but how to apply this on a big scale.
cues.zh: 现在，我认为问题已经不是它是否有效，而是如何大规模应用。

cues.en: Erika Santoro, speaking to Roland Pease.
cues.zh: 埃里卡·桑托罗接受罗兰·皮斯采访。

cues.en: We end here in the UK, where people living with Parkinson's disease have been benefiting from weekly table tennis sessions.
cues.zh: 我们最后来到英国，帕金森病患者一直从每周的乒乓球活动中受益。

cues.en: The BBC's Mark Norman has been to the Brighton Table Tennis Club to find out more.
cues.zh: BBC记者马克·诺曼前往布莱顿乒乓球俱乐部了解更多情况。

cues.en: People living with Parkinson's disease have described the benefits of playing table tennis as a no-brainer.
cues.zh: 帕金森病患者说，打乒乓球带来的好处显而易见。

cues.en: They say it improves their movement, mood and confidence.
cues.zh: 他们说，这能改善运动能力、情绪和自信。

cues.en: Playing on the tables today are a few volunteers, but also a range of people living with Parkinson's.
cues.zh: 今天在球台旁活动的有几名志愿者，也有不同情况的帕金森病患者。

cues.en: In a moment, we'll hear from Richard Witts, an emeritus professor of music and sound, diagnosed with Parkinson's five years ago.
cues.zh: 稍后我们将听到理查德·威茨的讲述。他是音乐与声音荣休教授，五年前被诊断患有帕金森病。

cues.en: But first, here's David Priest, a former restaurant worker, diagnosed 15 years ago.
cues.zh: 但首先请听大卫·普里斯的讲述。他曾是餐厅工作人员，15年前被诊断患病。

cues.en: So if I play like this session this morning, for most of the afternoon I'll feel my movement will improve, my mood will improve.
cues.zh: 所以，如果我像今天早上这样参加活动，我觉得整个下午运动能力和情绪都会改善。

cues.en: The main problem with Parkinson's is balance. You lose your sense of balance.
cues.zh: 帕金森病的主要问题是平衡。患者会失去平衡感。

cues.en: And so this table tennis helps to address this problem.
cues.zh: 所以打乒乓球有助于应对这个问题。

cues.en: Also playing at the tables today is Tracy Steele. He's a former maths teacher and was diagnosed five years ago.
cues.zh: 今天还在球台旁活动的有特雷西·斯蒂尔。他曾是数学老师，五年前被诊断患病。

cues.en: And finally, we will hear from Carol Gill. She's been living with Parkinson's for 11 years and is a former student administrator.
cues.zh: 最后，我们将听到卡罗尔·吉尔的讲述。她患帕金森病已有11年，曾任学生事务管理员。

cues.en: Got, like, you know, lots of people you can talk to, which is really useful, because you need people who've actually been there themselves, you know.
cues.zh: 你知道，这里有很多可以交谈的人，这很有用，因为你需要真正经历过这一切的人。

cues.en: You have to react so quickly and score and move and think about your tactics at the same time.
cues.zh: 你必须迅速反应、得分、移动，同时思考战术。

cues.en: So for people with Parkinson's, that's a really exceptional thing.
cues.zh: 所以对帕金森病患者来说，这真的非常特别。

cues.en: The Brighton Table Tennis Club hosts weekly sessions for people with Parkinson's, dementia and other neurological conditions.
cues.zh: 布莱顿乒乓球俱乐部每周为帕金森病、痴呆症和其他神经系统疾病患者举办活动。

cues.en: Here's the club's head of community outreach and the voice you may have heard shouting in the background, Nick Creal.
cues.zh: 下面是该俱乐部社区拓展负责人尼克·克里尔的声音，你可能听到他在背景中喊话。

cues.en: I firmly believe that this is a sport because of the quick decision-making you have to make with your brain.
cues.zh: 我坚信这是一项运动，因为你必须用大脑迅速作出决定。

cues.en: It massively has benefits in terms of slowing down the illness.
cues.zh: 这对延缓病情发展有非常大的益处。

cues.en: Parkinson's is a progressive disorder affecting the brain, nervous system and muscle control.
cues.zh: 帕金森病是一种进行性疾病，会影响大脑、神经系统和肌肉控制。

cues.en: There are around 150,000 people in the UK living with the condition.
cues.zh: 英国约有15万人患有这种疾病。

cues.en: Last year, Table Tennis England and Parkinson's UK announced a partnership to create more opportunities for people to play the sport.
cues.zh: 去年，英格兰乒乓球协会与英国帕金森病协会宣布建立合作关系，为人们创造更多参加这项运动的机会。

cues.en: Philip Lindley is from Parkinson's UK.
cues.zh: 菲利普·林德利来自英国帕金森病协会。

cues.en: Table tennis is shown to have many benefits for things like balance and coordination.
cues.zh: 研究显示，乒乓球在平衡和协调等方面有许多益处。

cues.en: It can also be really good for memory, and it's also been really beneficial for social interaction as well.
cues.zh: 它对记忆力也很有帮助，对社交互动同样非常有益。

cues.en: Table Tennis England recognise the sport's power to support people and want everyone to feel there's a place at the table tennis table.
cues.zh: 英格兰乒乓球协会认识到这项运动支持患者的力量，希望每个人都能在乒乓球台前找到位置。

cues.en: That report was from Mark Norman.
cues.zh: 以上报道来自马克·诺曼。

cues.en: And that's all from the Happy Pod for now. We'd love to hear from you. As ever, the address is globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk.
cues.zh: 本期《Happy Pod》到此结束。欢迎来信，邮箱是 globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk。

cues.en: The editor of this edition is Karen Martin. I am Holly Gibbs. Until next time, goodbye.
cues.zh: 本期编辑是凯伦·马丁。我是霍莉·吉布斯。下期再见。
